definitions.explanation: The ability to withstand wear, pressure, or damage over time. Used for both physical objects and human endurance.

examples.japanese: {耐久性|たいきゅうせい}に{優|すぐ}れた{素材|そざい}だ。
examples.english: It's a material with excellent durability.

examples.japanese: この{製品|せいひん}は{耐久|たいきゅう}テストに{合格|ごうかく}している。
examples.english: This product has passed durability testing.

examples.japanese: {耐久|たいきゅう}レースでは{体力|たいりょく}だけでなく{精神力|せいしんりょく}も{試|ため}される。
examples.english: In endurance races, not only physical strength but also mental fortitude is tested.

notes: Almost always appears in compounds or as a modifier: {耐久性|たいきゅうせい} (durability — the most common form), {耐久|たいきゅう}{消費財|しょうひざい} (durable consumer goods), {耐久|たいきゅう}レース (endurance race), {耐久|たいきゅう}{年数|ねんすう} (service life, expected lifespan). The prefix {耐|たい}～ means "resistant to" and appears in: {耐水|たいすい} (waterproof), {耐熱|たいねつ} (heat-resistant), {耐震|たいしん} (earthquake-resistant). Related: {丈夫|じょうぶ} (sturdy — everyday word for toughness), {頑丈|がんじょう} (robust).
